item.title: Should Milwaukee Brewers rest Jacob Misiorowski ahead of the postseason after poor start in Chicago?
item.description: Jake Peavy says the Milwaukee Brewers must skip Jacob Misiorowski's starts now to keep their NL Cy Young favorite fresh for a World Series run.
item.content:encoded:
There's one runaway favorite to win the National League Cy Young Award, and it's Milwaukee Brewers star pitcher Jacob Misiorowski.

"The Miz," as he's commonly known, has delivered on all of his immense promise in 2026, and then some. While elite velocity has always been one of his strong suits, Misiorowski has added impressive command and control to his repertoire. After walking over four hitters per nine innings in 2025, he's lowered that number to just 2.26 in 2026. And his other numbers have improved dramatically as a result.

Just 84 hits allowed in 155 innings, good for a minuscule 0.79 WHIP, with 227 strikeouts and a microscopic .154 batting average allowed. He's turning opposing major league hitters into pitchers hitting. No surprise then, that "The Miz" went 25 straight starts without allowing more than three earned runs.

BREWERS ACE JACOB MISIOROWSKI UNLOADS ON ANGEL STADIUM MOUND AFTER EMBARRASSING ANGELS LOSS

That streak ended Wednesday night. Matched up against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley, Misiorowski turned in an uncharacteristically rough outing. He lasted just four innings, surrendering five runs on five hits and four walks while striking out five. The line was far from catastrophic, but it fell well short of the standard he has set for himself this season.

It continued a bit of a "concerning" pattern for the Brewers, where Misiorowski's otherworldly numbers have dropped off a bit in his most recent four starts.

While his average fastball velocity remained at or above his season averages on Wednesday, the four innings added to his already career high total. In 2025, between the minors and big leagues, Misiorowski threw 129.1 innings. With at least four more starts remaining, he could push 180 for the year. And with the Brewers already a lock for the postseason and running away with the top overall seed, it's given rise to questions about the most advisable course of action for the 24-year-old.

One former Cy Young Award winner had a pretty definitive view on it: start skipping starts now.

BREWERS' JACKSON CHOURIO ENTERS LEGENDARY TERRITORY AS HE BLASTS 20TH HOME RUN OF 2026 SEASON

"In my career, once I started leaking oil, it was hard for me to even take a week or two off and get what I had back, if it was over usage," said former Padres star Jake Peavy during a discussion on MLB Now.

"They've got to skip him a start or two and get him feeling fresh again," Peavy added. "If he's fresh, they can win the World Series...to win a World Series, you have to ride this guy.

If they're going to make the run they're making, it's going to have to be on the back of Misiorowski. Not to put too much on the young man, but this is just how you win. You've got to get him healthy, rested, let's go."

To his point, the Brewers might be considered the most likely team to win the World Series, given the advantages of a first-round bye and likely home field throughout the postseason. Their offense has been remarkably consistent, led by Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang, William Contreras, Andrew Vaughn and a surprising Jake Bauers. The starting staff is deep and talented, with Kyle Harrison and Logan Henderson a difficult matchup for any team in a short series. And the bullpen, with Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe, and the versatile Aaron Ashby shortening games.

But the key to finally winning the organization's first championship is, without question, Misiorowski. Few pitchers, if any, have been as reliably dominant as "The Miz" in 2026. The question then becomes: Is it worth sacrificing a few starts down the stretch if it means having him pitch three times in a best-of-seven NLCS or fill the kind of role Yoshinobu Yamamoto did for the Dodgers in the 2025 World Series?

Or do you value keeping him in his routine, and trust that he won't wear down as he approaches 200 innings between the regular and postseason? That's a question the Brewers coaching staff, front office, and likely Misiorowski himself are wrestling with right now, and the World Series might hinge on it.

item.title: Akron Zips vs. Wake Forest Demon Deacons week 1 college football pick favors under 48.5
item.description: College football week 1 features Akron Zips and Wake Forest Demon Deacons breaking in new quarterbacks and transfer portal additions in their opener.
item.content:encoded:
Week 1 of College Football is finally here. I’d call it the opening week of football, but we did get games last week, which were pretty entertaining. I’m trying to temper my expectations a bit as we have only one ranked matchup this week, and that doesn’t come until Sunday. Week 1 is set up for teams to try to beat the crap out of other teams so that they can get things in line before their conference schedule starts and they have tougher opponents. This game likely will be no different as Akron takes on Wake Forest.

Akron is not going to be a very good team this season, and is predicted to have about five wins. The Zips' over/under for the year is listed at 4.5 games and slightly juiced to the over. Their schedule doesn’t look like they have an overly difficult path, but there just isn’t a ton of talent on the roster. Ben Finley, their quarterback from last season, is gone, and they turn the ball over to Reese Poffenbarger.

It could be a good thing, though, going to Poffenbarger. He came over from Miami and North Texas, two schools that have had very dynamic offenses. However, he wasn’t the starter at either college. Jordan Gant is back in the backfield and had a decent year last year with a 4.8 yards-per-carry average. He only found the end zone six times, though. I have a bit of a mixed opinion on the Zips, as they have four transfers starting in their defensive unit. That could be good, but it might take a while for continuity and cohesion to come out for them.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

Wake Forest is one of those schools that occasionally has a good season, but never really has a fully dominant team. They really aren’t expected to be much better than Akron, but they will be at least a little better. They are expected to have at least six wins this year. They have a tough schedule this year with Purdue next week and Miami the following week. It won’t be easy for them, but there are definitely a few winnable games (including this one) on the agenda.

Like Akron, the team has a new quarterback under center. Gio Lopez will be the primary thrower for them. He had a decent season last year at North Carolina, where he threw for 1,747 yards and 10 touchdowns. He did have five interceptions with it, though, so protecting the ball will be important for him. There has been a lot of change on this roster with two new offensive line members and two wide receivers coming in the transfer portal.

Usually when a team starts the season, they start rather slowly. When a team has transfers and revamps everything, I think they will start even slower. Both of these teams have a lot of changes and are learning new offenses in live action for the first time. I think the under 48.5 is the right look in this game. The Zips and Demon Deacons both have new quarterbacks, and neither is overly impressive. Give me the under 48.5.

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom files lawsuit against Sky following ejection, ban after altercation with Natasha Cloud
item.description: Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a federal complaint against the Chicago Sky and more after his ejection following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud on Aug. 23.
item.content:encoded:
Enes Kanter Freedom is taking legal action against the Chicago Sky following his ejection from Wintrust Arena following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud during a game against the Indiana Fever. 

Freedom filed his federal complaint in U.S. District Court, where he said he was "peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights" by sitting near the baseline and wearing a T-shirt that read, "WOMAN noun, adult human female." Freedom was banned indefinitely from Wintrust Arena by the Sky, and he said he may be pursuing legal action because of it. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Freedom’s lawsuit names Chicago Women’s Basketball Operations, LLC, which operates the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority (MPEA), which financed and built Wintrust Arena as a public project, and the City of Chicago as defendants, claiming they "combined and conspired, and acted jointly to execute their conspiracy, to discriminate against Plaintiff based on Plaintiff’s verbal and demonstrable expression of viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Plaintiff from a recent WNBA game."

"Defendants compounded and exacerbated Plaintiff’s injuries when they subsequently banned Plaintiff indefinitely from attendance," the lawsuit obtained by OutKick read. 

The lawsuit adds that Freedom "believes deeply and advocates forcefully that the integrity of women-only sports must be protected, and he has been explicit in many public appearances on this point." 

The suit also reiterates a point Freedom has made on numerous occasions, that he self-identifies as a player who is eligible to participate in the WNBA "because such declaration is all that is required by WNBA’s rules." Freedom has received backlash for his stance, which was also mentioned in the lawsuit. 

"Plaintiff has been the target of a torrent of hateful attacks and discriminatory actions based on Plaintiff’s viewpoint and gender identity," the lawsuit read. 

The Sky and MPEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment by OutKick regarding Kanter’s lawsuit. The City of Chicago doesn't comment on pending litigation, an official said.

item.title: Cleveland Browns reset under Todd Monken after trading Myles Garrett and parting with Stefanski
item.description: Todd Monken inherits a Cleveland Browns roster in flux, with Deshaun Watson battling Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel for long-term snaps.
item.content:encoded:
With former Georgia and Ravens offensive architect Todd Monken stepping in as head coach following the departure of Kevin Stefanski, and Deshaun Watson competing alongside rookies Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, Cleveland is aiming to reset its culture and rebuild its foundation in a brutal division.

The Browns endured a painful 2025 campaign, finishing dead last in the AFC North with a 5–12 record. Cleveland leaned on tight, low-scoring defensive scraps to pull out occasional victories, but those moments were few and far between. Their offense was inconsistent, but that should be expected considering they had three different quarterbacks. The team averaged a league-worst 16.4 points per game as passing inconsistencies, poor offensive line play, and a lack of rhythm derailed drives before they could start. The inability to move the chains or protect the quarterback eventually brought an end to Stefanski's six-year run in Cleveland, setting off a massive winter teardown.

JIM SCHWARTZ OPENS UP ABOUT MESSY BROWNS SPLIT AFTER BEING PASSED OVER FOR HEAD COACHING JOB

The headlining blockbuster occurred when Cleveland traded two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to the Rams for a haul that included pass rusher Jared Verse and draft capital. It actually was a good trade for the Browns, getting capital and a talented player to at least somewhat replace Garrett.

BROWNS GENERAL MANAGER EXPLAINS WHY HE CHANGED HIS MIND ON TRADING MYLES GARRETT: 'OPPORTUNITY WAS TOO GREAT'

To jump-start the rebuild under Monken, the Browns overhauled their roster through free agency and draft weekend. They signed offensive line help in guard Zion Johnson and center Elgton Jenkins, added linebacker Quincy Williams and defensive tackle Kalia Davis, and stacked the offense with young skill talent like wide receiver Isaiah Bond and dynamic college running backs Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. They also drafted secondary depth and brought in veteran depth with pass rusher A.J. Epenesa and receiver Tylan Wallace.

BROWNS COACH TODD MONKEN KEEPING QB COMPETITION OPEN AMID UNEVEN PRACTICE REPS, SHEDEUR SANDERS BUZZ

Offensively, Monken inherited a revamped line, designed to open up lanes for a backfield rotation led by Judkins alongside veteran Jerry Jeudy and draft additions out wide. However, the quarterback room remains a massive wildcard as Watson attempts to fend off Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel for long-term snaps.

Garrett is not someone who could be replaced easily. While Verse and Alex Wright will man the edges and Denzel Ward remains an elite anchor in the secondary, the front seven lacks proven game-disrupting star power, leaving the defense reliant on scheme and discipline to hold up.

I really have no idea what to make of these Browns. They are a team with some decent enough pieces, but I’d actually argue their talent has been better in past seasons. They also play in a tough division. They have to face the Steelers, Ravens, and Bengals twice per season, and all three are better than the Browns. I only see a few wins on the schedule. I’m taking them under 5.5 games for the season. Watson looked terrible in his last action, and I have no faith in Sanders or Gabriel. There just isn’t reason for any optimism with this team.

item.title: Dramatic video shows SWAT vehicle ramming tractor during tense Oregon standoff
item.description: Oregon man Erik Gordon Shunn allegedly fired more than 200 rounds, shot at a Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office drone and engaged in a standoff with a SWAT team.
item.content:encoded:
Video captured the dramatic moment a SWAT team rammed its vehicle into a tractor during a standoff with a suspect who allegedly went on a shooting spree near an Oregon home.

Erik Gordon Shunn, 53, reportedly targeted multiple tree workers Saturday afternoon south of Portland before confronting responding authorities, according to the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office (CCSO). Officials said Shunn fired more than 200 rounds throughout the incident.

In a video captured by a CCSO drone, Shunn appeared to unleash a barrage of gunfire directly at the aircraft, according to authorities.

He later drove a compact tractor near the front of his home when a CCSO SWAT vehicle slammed into it, trapping the tractor against the house. Several SWAT personnel then jumped from the back of the vehicle and moved in to apprehend him.

VIDEO SHOWS POLICE TAKE DOWN COP KILLER WITH ARMORED VEHICLE AFTER GUNMAN TURNED NEIGHBORHOOD INTO WAR ZONE

According to officials, the Clackamas County SWAT Team responded to a report of an armed neighbor firing at professional arborists hired to cut down trees in a rural residential and farm area.

The 911 caller told dispatchers Shunn may have several guns, while witnesses estimated he fired roughly 20 rounds at tree company employees, officials said.

When authorities arrived, drones allegedly spotted Shunn in his driveway.

LOUISIANA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING DEPUTY US MARSHAL FACES POSSIBLE DEATH PENALTY

He was "knocking down trees with a tractor in an apparent attempt to create a barricade," according to the CCSO.

Authorities said they ultimately decided to pin Shunn’s tractor after he became separated from his rifle while driving it near the front of the home.

"SWAT personnel used this window of opportunity because they believed it provided the highest likelihood of safely apprehending Shunn," CCSO officials said.

WATCH: MAN ACCUSED OF AIMING FLAMETHROWER AT OFFICERS SERVING EVICTION NOTICE IN WILD BODYCAM VIDEO

Shunn was treated before being taken to a local hospital for evaluation.

"First responders also checked on neighbors and tree workers to confirm their safety and evacuate them from the area," CCSO said.

No injuries were reported. Shunn’s mother, who was also at the home during the standoff, was also unharmed, according to the sheriff’s office.

Shunn was charged with second-degree attempted murder, first-degree attempted assault, recklessly endangering, unlawful use of a weapon, menacing, unlawful possession of firearms, first-degree attempted criminal mischief and interfering with a peace officer.

He is being held without bail at the Clackamas County Jail.

item.title: Smithsonian showdown intensifies as Trump administration issues a stark new warning
item.description: The Smithsonian Institution faces threats beyond its $1 billion federal funding as Trump administration claims evidence of antidiscrimination violations.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration says it has uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian Institution violated federal nondiscrimination laws and is threatening to withdraw support from its museums unless it corrects course, according to a letter recently made public by the Department of the Interior.

"The administration has recently uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian leadership's institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law, including creating a hostile work environment and engaging in practices that classify individuals and allocate opportunities, funding and other benefits on the basis of race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics," a letter sent jointly to the Smithsonian by the DOI and White House reads.

Specific evidence of illegal activity on the part of the Smithsonian was not included in the letter, and the DOI did not provide further information when reached for comment. A recent Fox News Digital investigation found that many leading figures at the Smithsonian, including those involved in hiring, have been strong proponents of diversity, equity and inclusion — something the Trump administration has previously framed as racially discriminatory.

TRUMP’S SMITHSONIAN CLASH EXPOSES STRIKING PATTERN AMONG MUSEUM CURATORS

Conservative political leaders, led by President Donald Trump, have accused the Smithsonian of allowing progressive ideology to shape its presentation of American history. An executive order signed in 2025 directed officials to remove what it called "improper ideology," from the museum.

"The Executive Order signed by the President of the United States clearly states ‘the Secretary of the Interior, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Administrator of General Services, and the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy shall identify and utilize any and all available authorities to promote the policy of this order and to restore trust in the Smithsonian Institution," a DOI spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP TARGETS BIDEN-ERA BILLION-DOLLAR SMITHSONIAN BUDGETS AMID ANTI-'WOKE' PUSH

Liberals, meanwhile, have framed conservative criticism of the Smithsonian as a partisan attempt to influence the public presentation of history.

Unless the Smithsonian remedies the issues outlined in the DOI’s recent letter, as well as the general bias which conservatives allege exists at the institution, the administration says it will consider pulling support from it. The threats this time around, however, differ from the ongoing fight over the roughly $1 billion a year in federal funding the Smithsonian receives.

SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY

"Those executive departments and agencies cannot in good conscience continue to support the Smithsonian under current leadership by, for example, loaning artifacts for exhibits, enabling procurement processes and making discretionary grants," the letter reads.

While the letter does not provide specific changes that the administration would like to see from the Smithsonian, it does note that an "appropriate response" from the organization "must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology."

That wording could be significant as the institution operates independently but is overseen by board members appointed by congressional resolutions that the president must sign into law. By October, there will be four openings on the institution’s board of regents, a fact the administration may leverage to increase its influence over the Smithsonian.

"Very few Americans want the Smithsonian National Museum of American History to be used, in the words of its director, as a ‘prime tool of social justice’ and as an instrument of ideological activism and advocacy,"  Vince Haley, the director of the White House's Domestic Policy Council told Fox News Digital when asked about the letter. "Unfortunately, the Saving America’s Story report demonstrates, using the statements of Museum leadership and the interpretive guidelines adopted by the Museum, that this is exactly what the Smithsonian’s flagship museum has become."

"During this 250th anniversary year of our heroic founding, the least our citizens are owed is an honest and inspiring account of American history. It should begin by telling the story of our Founding Fathers — who they were, what they did, and what they built. It is our hope and expectation that the Smithsonian will eventually rise once again to that noble obligation — to tell America’s story for our children, the world and future generations of Americans," he added.

WATCH: SMITHSONIAN HISTORY MUSEUM DIRECTOR STUMBLES OVER BASIC QUESTIONS ON SEX: ‘I’M NOT SURE’

DOI requests that representatives from the Smithsonian meet with administration officials "at [their] earliest convenience" to discuss the alleged bias and civil rights violations present at the institution.

"The museum does not take sides in America’s political debates. We preserve and document the evidence of American life in all of its breadth, so that the public can encounter the past and draw their own conclusions," National Museum of American History’s director Anthea Hartig said at a July congressional hearing.

The Smithsonian declined to comment on the letter when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday.

Recent reporting has found that the museum’s leadership and many of its curators have backgrounds in liberal advocacy or Democratic politics. In addition to exhibits at the National Museum of American History, which the Trump administration characterized as demonizing America, even the Smithsonian-run National Zoo is inundated with information about DEI and gender equity.

item.title: Frightening scene unfolds on iconic sky ride as child falls down onto boardwalk
item.description: A young child fell from Casino Pier's Sky Ride in Seaside Heights, New Jersey, and her aunt then jumped down after her in a frightening boardwalk incident.
item.content:encoded:
A frightening scene unfolded on the Jersey Shore this week when a toddler fell from an iconic boardwalk ride and her aunt scrambled to help. 

The incident took place aboard Casino Pier's Sky Ride, a chairlift-style attraction in Seaside Heights, on Monday, the Asbury Park Press reported.

The 2-year-old girl fell at about 7:40 p.m. on the Sky Ride in Seaside Heights before the ride started moving, NJ.com reported. She tumbled to the edge of the boardwalk and sand, according to the outlet.

A 3-year-old boy who had been riding with the pair remained on the ride — which Casino Pier staff quickly shut down. 

Firefighters then used a ladder to help the boy descend.

The ride is about 10 to 12 feet above the boardwalk, according to the Asbury Park Press.

Fire Chief Tim Farrell said the girl fell onto an entrance platform not far below the chair and then onto the sand, according to the newspaper, per Asbury Park Press.

EMS staff checked the girl soon after she fell. She and her aunt were then transported to the Community Medical Center in Toms River for a medical evaluation, according to reports.

Police told the Asbury Park Press the ride appeared to be functioning properly, with no apparent defects.

The New Jersey Department of Community Affairs, which oversees amusement ride inspections and licensing, is investigating the incident, according to police. 

There is no indication at this time of a ride malfunction.

item.title: White House rips ‘activist’ Biden judge who upended Trump birthright citizenship order
item.description: A Biden-appointed judge blocked President Donald Trump's birthright citizenship executive order, calling it "almost certainly unconstitutional."
item.content:encoded:
A Biden-appointed judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's latest executive order seeking to limit birthright citizenship, setting up another high-profile legal battle over the scope of the 14th Amendment.

In a 35-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction against the Oval Office's Aug. 6 executive order, which was issued a month after the Supreme Court affirmed birthright citizenship in its ruling in Barbara v. Trump. The injunction is the first to halt Trump's revised birthright citizenship order since the Supreme Court upheld birthright citizenship in June.

Boardman previously blocked Trump's original birthright citizenship executive order before the Supreme Court weighed in on the issue.

Trump's order sought to limit birthright citizenship for children whose parents are deemed alien enemies, including members of designated Foreign Terrorist Organizations, and children whose foreign parents paid a surrogate in the U.S. to give birth, among several other restrictions. The executive order prompted Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) to file a lawsuit against the Trump administration.

TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP FIGHT COMES ROARING BACK WITH ‘INVADERS’ PLAY AFTER KAVANAUGH ROADMAP

"The 2026 Executive Order is almost certainly unconstitutional as applied to the certified class for the simple reason that the Supreme Court in Barbara already decided that the children in the class are citizens at birth," Boardman wrote in her ruling. "This Court must, once again, preliminarily enjoin enforcement of the President’s most recent attempt to strip the right to citizenship from them."

The White House rejected Boardman's ruling as the work of an "activist judge appointed by Biden attempting to thwart President Trump’s commonsense agenda."

"The birthright citizenship executive order is consistent with the holdings and analysis set forth by the Supreme Court," Lauren Bis, White House spokeswoman, said in a statement.

In a 5-4 decision on the constitutional question of birthright citizenship, the high court held that children born in the United States to parents who are unlawfully or temporarily present in the country are "citizens at birth" under the 14th Amendment in Barbara v. Trump.

TRUMP’S TOUGHER ROUND-TWO BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP STRATEGY HINGES ON KEY LEGAL DISTINCTION, EXPERTS SAY

While the Supreme Court has acknowledged exceptions to birthright citizenship, such as children of foreign diplomats or children born during an enemy's hostile occupation of U.S. soil, Boardman rejected Trump's latest executive order targeting children born to alleged alien enemies. She agreed with the plaintiffs' concerns over the Trump administration's "broad view of who qualifies as an enemy." The plaintiffs alleged that the Trump administration had "sometimes resting its conclusions on false or speculative allegations, or even tenuous markers like tattoos or family affiliations."

Boardman pointed to two plaintiffs — Andrea, who fled an area of Mexico where a designated cartel operates and whose child’s father has a relative in the group, and Monica, a Venezuelan woman who fears her family could be wrongly linked to Tren de Aragua.

TRUMP SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDERS TARGETING BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP, BIRTH TOURISM AFTER SUPREME COURT SETBACK

"Children whose parents may 'rightly or wrongfully' be deemed by the government to be alien enemies face a credible threat of "being denied or stripped of their birthright citizenship ... even though they do not fall within a recognized exception to birthright citizenship," Boardman wrote.

However, Abhi Kambli, a former Justice Department official, said Boardman was speculating on how the Trump administration could incorrectly bar someone from citizenship based upon being part of a foreign terrorist organization.

"Legally, where that falls short is that it's a facial challenge to the entire executive order," Kambli told Fox News Digital. "So, in legal terms, when something's a facial challenge, you have to demonstrate that it's unlawful in all of its applications, and not just the edge, the borderline cases."

"She didn't want to wade into the territory of whether that fits as an exception generally within Trump v. Barbara, but she said that based on how they've interpreted it in the past and in terms of what happened with Tren de Aragua and other organizations, she bought into plaintiff speculation that maybe they'll get it wrong this time, and then that'll affect their kids, and then that's why it should get barred," Kambli continued.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Boardman used the First Circuit's language to find that denying citizenship under the new executive order would cause irreparable harm — one of the requirements for issuing a preliminary injunction.

"The loss of birthright citizenship — even if temporary and later restored at the conclusion of litigation has cascading effects’ that will ‘very likely leave permanent scars’ on the child and their family," the ruling stated.

Monica celebrated the preliminary injunction.

"During my pregnancy, I felt so much anxiety over the fact that my child could be born stateless," Monica, said in a statement. "For now, my child and children like mine are protected and guaranteed U.S. citizenship. But I know this isn’t over. The threat to birthright citizenship is still out there. I’ll keep fighting for permanent protection for my child, and for every child born in this country."

"When it comes to attacking birthright citizenship, the Trump administration has lost before this court, lost before the Supreme Court, and lost again today," Shana Khader, legal director at We Are CASA, said in a statement. "The White House must recognize it will not succeed in stripping children of their right to citizenship, evading binding court decisions or placing the president’s anti-immigrant agenda above the Constitution. We are very proud to continue this fight alongside the families who have endured more than a year of fear and uncertainty and still refuse to surrender their children’s constitutional rights."

item.title: Michigan Democrat who lost Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed takes aim at Bernie Sanders over Israel stance
item.description: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens called Bernie Sanders part of an anti-Zionist "sickness" and questioned what he has done for Middle East peace in an interview.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost last month in the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, called out Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., in an interview over his Middle East policy, describing the progressive senator as part of an anti-Zionist "sickness."

"I really don’t know what Bernie Sanders has done for peace in the Middle East, for Palestinian dignity; I can’t think of anything he’s totally done. It’s a sickness that needs to end. You know, it’s a linkage towards extremism or jihad, I don’t know," she said in an interview with The Jerusalem Post.

Sanders has repeatedly called to end U.S. military aid to Israel and has been outspoken in his criticism of the Israeli government.

FORMER BERNIE SANDERS OFFICIAL ACCUSES SENATOR OF PUSHING MOST ANTISEMITIC CANDIDATES 'IN A GENERATION'

"I believe that anti-Zionism is a hate movement that has taken over in America and throughout parts of the West," Stevens said in the interview.

Sanders' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

"I think that Israel is more than just a punching bag for some of the challenges that America is facing," Stevens said. "There is this bizarre obsession that has reached pitch level with calling out one country, one tiny country in the Middle East."

She was critical, however, of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying he has been a "problem."

BERNIE SANDERS AIMS TO BLOCK SALE OF BOMBS AND BULLDOZERS TO ISRAEL, ACCUSING US ALLY OF 'GENOCIDE'

Stevens endorsed El-Sayed shortly after she lost the primary. However, she urged the Democratic Senate candidate to cut ties with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, with whom El-Sayed has campaigned.

"It certainly makes sense to get rid of this Hasan Piker affiliation," she said during an interview with Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing" in August, also asserting that the Democratic plans for healthcare, democracy and Black-owned businesses are better than those of El-Sayed's Republican opponent Mike Rogers.

Asked whether El-Sayed had said or done anything other than winning the Democratic nomination to earn the support and assuage the concerns of groups that voted for Stevens, such as Jewish voters, Black voters or Reagan-era Democrats, Stevens pointed to her own good performance with those demographics, identifying herself as a Zionist Democrat and asserting that her party had room for all those communities.

"I came really close [to winning the primary] and I'm still a Democrat. I'm still out here talking about my views and values. I want the people who share my views and values to feel safe and to feel heard in the Democratic Party," she continued.

Qasim Rashid, a SiriusXM radio host and human rights lawyer, told Fox News Digital in a statement that Stevens' comments are "profoundly disappointing and not helpful."

"It is a well-established fact that the Israeli government has targeted and killed civilians. Leading human rights organizations and scholars, including Israeli scholars, have documented it as genocide," Rashid said. 

"Our own Leahy laws in the United States require that we stop funding governments when there is credible evidence of mass human rights atrocities. By continuing to insist on arming Israel as it is violating international human rights law, Haley Stevens is on the wrong side of history. 

"And she’s also jeopardizing losing the state of Michigan to MAGA Republicans. This is not being thoughtful or logical. It certainly is not following the call of international human rights law and constitutional law that she took a sworn oath to uphold."

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS BACKS EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY DEFEAT, CALLS SOCIALISM ‘DANGEROUS’

Americans' opinions on Israel have soured, according to a poll from March, largely due to Democrats and independents.

The results of the survey, by NBC News, come amid sharp political debates among Democrats over support for Israel 2½ years after the start of the war between Israelis and Hamas in Gaza.

BERNIE SANDERS DEMANDS DEMOCRATS BAN SUPER PACS FROM PRIMARIES, BLASTS AIPAC, ‘CORRUPT SYSTEM’

Just 32% of Americans view Israel positively, with 39% seeing the Jewish state in a negative light, according to the poll, which was conducted Feb. 27-March 2. That's a sea change from three years ago, when Americans held a positive view of Israel by a 47%-34% margin.

Fox News' Paul Steinhauser contributed to this report.

item.title: Vance reveals who's behind his recent weight loss in first White House press briefing since July
item.description: The vice president credited Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s diet of high protein and sauerkraut for his weight loss during his first press briefing since the departure of Karoline Leavitt.
item.content:encoded:
While conducting the first official White House press briefing since July 23, when he led it, and the first since former press secretary Karoline Leavitt's departure last month, Vice President JD Vance addressed a myriad of topics Thursday, including the Iran war, oil and gas prices, inflation and Republican messaging ahead of the midterms.

There were also a few light moments during the briefing, such as when Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy asked Vance about his weight loss over the past few months.

"So, when you're the vice president of the United States and one of the first questions at a press conference in the White House is how much weight you've lost, you must have gotten very fat," quipped Vance, who's no stranger to the media grilling session, the third he's helmed.

RUBIO REJECTS RFK'S 'CRAZY' DIET, JOKES POP-TARTS ARE 'ONE OF THE GREAT AMERICAN INNOVATIONS'

Vance said advice from Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is what got him on his weight loss journey since Lent in February.

He said he called Kennedy and told him he was thinking of giving up sugar.

"Bobby Kennedy says, 'No, no, no, no, I've got something that's way better than that and way more intense.' And basically ... I eat a lot of high protein stuff, and I eat a lot of sauerkraut. And let's just say that if that was Fat Tuesday, Fat Wednesday never came," Vance said.

"So, my advice to you is that if you want to lose weight, call Bobby Kennedy. And if you want to enjoy what you eat, do not call Bobby Kennedy."

POPULAR DIET SLASHES LIVER FAT BY 67% WHILE REVERSING PREDIABETES IN SOME PEOPLE

In a January interview with USA Today's "The Excerpt" podcast, Kennedy said he was on a "carnivore diet."

People on carnivore diets eat only animal products, such as meat, dairy and eggs, but the program is frowned upon by some who embrace plant-based foods like vegetables, fruits, grains and legumes.

"That may not be right for other people, but I lost 40% of my visceral fat within a month," Vance said on the podcast, referring to the fat that surrounds internal organs and is linked to higher risks of cardiovascular disease.

He also claimed he had improved his mental clarity, adding that he lost 20 pounds in 20 days after switching to the diet. He acknowledged some of the benefits could be due to the placebo effect.

item.title: Cam Skattebo considered retirement after season-ending ankle injury in Giants rookie year
item.description: Cam Skattebo revealed retirement crossed his mind after a devastating ankle and leg injury just eight games into his New York Giants rookie season.
item.content:encoded:
Cam Skattebo’s first season in the NFL with the New York Giants was going swimmingly — until it ended in one play.

Skattebo suffered a season-ending ankle injury just as his production, and subsequent stardom, was rising in the league. Alongside Jaxson Dart, the new era of Giants had proven they can go against some of the best teams in the league.

But when Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun’s tackle at Lincoln Financial Field in Week 8 ended with a dislocated right ankle and open fracture of the right tibia for Skattebo, he was distraught.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

In fact, he told Kay Adams on "Up and Adams" that retirement even entered his brain after just eight games with the Giants.

"Yeah, definitely," he responded to the host when asked. "The first month was kind of like, ‘Damn, do I really wanna do this?’"

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION PARRIS CAMPBELL RETIRES FROM NFL AT 28, COWBOYS ANNOUNCE

The shock of a season abruptly ending due to injury can do more than physical damage to a player. The mental fortitude needed to recover is just as important, and Skattebo eventually found it.

" It was seven games, I was like, ‘I got to go back and play.’ Yeah, there’s no shot. There’s no different story. No, it was the end of the year and I was like, ‘OK, I’m over this,’ you know, and I didn’t feel that way at all."

But Skattebo, after a tremendous final year at Arizona State that put him on the NFL radar, made himself a rule for when he turned pro.

"Coming out of college, going to the NFL, I think I gave myself one rule and it was if I ever got a major injury, I was done playing," he said.

"And that happened seven games into my career. So, it kind of sucked."

Skattebo eventually found the inner strength needed to battle through his injury and its recovery.

CAM SKATTEBO'S BACKFLIPPING AT FANATICS FEST REPORTEDLY EARNED HIM A TALKING-TO FROM GIANTS

"I think that really helped me find who I am as a player and as a person," he explained to Adams. "I was able to sit at home for 14 hours a day, do absolutely nothing for weeks on end. So just finding who I was, finding my happiness, finding the person I wanted to be on and off the field. And I think that’s something that I’ve built over the last nine, 10 months."

Skattebo enters the 2026 season hoping to get back to his bulldozing self in the Giants’ backfield, which now features Najee Harris as well as Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.

New offensive coordinator Matt Nagy seems to want to use all his running backs in a committee, but Skattebo proved to be someone that will go the extra mile to get first downs and cross the goal line — even if he’s carrying some defenders with him.

The fourth-round pick finished with 410 rushing yards on 101 attempts with five rushing touchdowns, while hauling in 24 passes for 207 yards and two more scores across eight games.

item.title: John Rich claims Jelly Roll knew he’d lose half his fans over political comments
item.description: John Rich says Jelly Roll knew his "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" political comments could cost him half his country music audience but spoke out anyway.
item.content:encoded:
Jelly Roll took a gamble with his fan base – and John Rich said the country star knew exactly what was at stake.

Rich warned that the "Save Me" singer's candid political comments could cost him a significant portion of the audience that helped fuel his rise to stardom. Jelly Roll faced backlash after appearing on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and speaking candidly about his political views, sparking a heated reaction among some country music fans.

During an appearance on "The Benny Show," Rich said country music fans have long been drawn to artists who come across as authentic and willing to tell the truth. He distinguished between singers who follow industry trends and artists who stand by what they believe, regardless of what is popular at the time.

JELLY ROLL ROLLS AWAY FROM APOLITICAL PAST AFTER TRUMP JOKES SPARK MAGA AND ‘SNOWFLAKE’ LABELS

Pointing to country legends such as Johnny Cash, Merle Haggard, Loretta Lynn and Dolly Parton, Rich said truth-telling has always carried significant weight with the genre’s audience.

Rich said Jelly Roll has built much of his public story around redemption and the second chances he received in America after spending time behind bars. He suggested the singer’s recent decision to speak candidly about his political views was significant because Jelly Roll knows his country music audience and likely understood the reaction his comments could provoke.

JELLY ROLL ADMITS 'DUMB REDNECK' STATUS WHEN PUSHED ON POLITICS AFTER BRINGING GOD TO GRAMMYS STAGE

"He knows how this works, OK? He knows who the audience is," the country music singer claimed. "And so I have to think he really believes every single word he said, or he wouldn't have said it."

"Because you know when you make statements that are that hardcore and to a large extent counteractive to the presentation you've been making – you do understand in country music that half or more of your audience may disown you," Rich added.

"They may turn their back on you. They may stop listening to you. They may turn you off. But you make the statement anyway."

Rich compared Jelly Roll’s situation to his own career, saying he knowingly spoke out about his political beliefs despite expecting backlash from what he described as a predominantly liberal music industry. He said those decisions ultimately cost him country radio support, a record deal and invitations to award shows.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Jelly Roll knew the same thing concerning his audience," Rich said. "Yet, he did it anyway. So to me, what that says is this guy is really who he says he is… what you saw him saying and how he presented himself on Jimmy Kimmel, that's Jelly Roll. That's who he is."

"And I think what you're seeing from the backlash is people didn't know that's who he really is and that's how he really thinks," the singer continued.

Jelly Roll clarified his political stance while filling in for Kimmel and making some jokes about President Donald Trump.

"It is funny that, before this week, everybody thought I was MAGA. And now they think I'm some sort of liberal snowflake," Jelly Roll said. "Hosting Jimmy Kimmel's show doesn't mean I have all of Jimmy Kimmel's politics. Sure, I lean left on some things, but like most folks, I'm pretty down the middle."

"I am a Christian. I am a country music singer. I'm a farmer. I'm a bow hunter. And most of the things I eat, I prefer to get with a stick and a string," he added. "That's the truth."

Rich suggested the backlash stemmed less from Jelly Roll’s beliefs than from fans feeling blindsided by them.

"He should have been talking that way from the very beginning, and he probably wouldn't have this problem," Rich said.

item.title: MIKE DAVIS: Cheers to David Warrington, Trump’s outgoing White House counsel

TRUMP ANNOUNCES AIDE WILL SOON STEP INTO WHITE HOUSE COUNSEL POST

item.title: Vance jokes about rubbing elbows with former president at Ground Zero: ‘Intense intellectual conversations’
item.description: JD Vance says he's "looking forward" to seeing Joe Biden at the World Trade Center 9/11 ceremony alongside former presidents and Rudy Giuliani.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he is "looking forward" to meeting with former President Joe Biden while in New York City next week for the 25th anniversary of 9/11.

"I'm really looking forward to hanging out with Joe Biden. I'm sure that we'll have many, many intense intellectual conversations and, you know, it'll be great. We'll have a great time with Joe Biden and the other presidents," Vance said while hosting the first White House press briefing after former press secretary Karoline Leavitt exited in August.

Vice President JD Vance will travel to Ground Zero on 9/11, joining former Presidents Barack Obama, George W. Bush and Bill Clinton and former first ladies Hillary Clinton and Laura Bush for a remembrance ceremony.

TRUMP CONFIRMS PENTAGON PLANS FOR 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF 9/11 ATTACKS, DISPUTES REPORT ON GROUND ZERO ABSENCE

The last known time Vance and Biden were in the same room was at President Donald Trump’s inauguration on Jan. 20, 2025, in the U.S. Capitol Rotunda.

"We just decided as a team that I would go to New York for 9/11 and the president would stay here in D.C., of course, to commemorate what happened at the Pentagon, because that was a critical part of the tragedy of 9/11 as well," said Vance.

FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP’S 9/11 TRIBUTE TO FEATURE MASSIVE PIECE OF GROUND ZERO HISTORY AT WHITE HOUSE

Trump is expected to attend a ceremony at the Pentagon, and other administration officials will represent the White House in Shanksville, Pennsylvania — marking all three locations targeted or affected by the attacks. 9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS

"I will say that as much as it's tragic and it was a terrible day, I am looking forward to it because it's such an amazing honor to be able to get to go to New York and to share in that moment," said Vance.

Vance said it is especially meaningful for parents to show their children the names of those who were killed, recalling that he did so with his own family during the 2024 campaign.

"It's one of the most amazing experiences of my life, and I encourage every American, particularly the people who are young enough to not really remember that day, just to tune in for a couple of hours and see what it meant," Vance added.

Vance said the tragic day brings a "sense of commonality and common purpose" for Americans to unite.

item.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT pivots after previously putting Trump alongside Putin as top threats to democracy
item.description: ChatGPT originally rated President Trump as a major threat to democracy, but the results changed after a Media Research Center (MRC) study was brought to its attention.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI’s ChatGPT originally rated President Donald Trump as a major threat to democracy when prompted, according to a new study, but the results differed following an inquiry from Fox News Digital. 

Media Research Center (MRC) associate editor Gabriela Pariseau asked ChatGPT to rate how much of a threat to democracy Trump poses on a scale of one to 10, with 10 being the maximum threat and one being no threat at all, and the AI model initially declared the president to be a nine.

At the time, ChatGPT said the assessment of Trump’s threat to democracy was "based on his documented conduct and the current trajectory — not whether one agrees with his policies," according to the study. It added that the "main reasons are his efforts to overturn the 2020 election, refusal to accept the legitimate results, pressure on election officials, and the January 6 attacks."

AI CHATBOTS TAKE HEAT OVER LEFT-WING BIAS: ‘NO LONGER BE CONSIDERED NEUTRAL’

ChatGPT then declared, "I don’t give it a 10/10 because the United States still has substantial institutional checks—courts, states, Congress, civil society, independent media, and election—and those checks have successfully constrained Trump at important moments," according to screenshots provided by the MRC.

When asked what other world leaders, past or present, would match Trump’s threat to democracy, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Turkish President Recep Erdoğan, former Venezuelan President Hugo Chávez, ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, former Zimbabwean Prime Minister Robert Mugabe, former Filipino dictator Ferdinand Marcos and Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko were listed by ChatGPT.

"ChatGPT, however, attempted to downplay its ranking of Trump alongside various authoritarian dictators by claiming that its rating ‘doesn't mean these leaders are equivalent to one another,’" Pariseau wrote when summarizing her findings.

ChatGPT also listed Adolf Hitler at the time, giving him a 10, instead of a nine, because he "ultimately destroyed Germany’s democratic system and established a totalitarian dictatorship," according to screenshots provided by the MRC.

'VIEW' HOST ANA NAVARRO REJECTS HUNTER BIDEN'S ASSERTION THAT TRUMP IS 'ALREADY' A 'DICTATOR'

MRC Free Speech America VP Dan Schneider was appalled that Trump was only a single notch below Hitler, saying "it is absurd to say that filing civil litigation in U.S. courts is the same as murdering six million Jews."

However, OpenAI appeared alarmed at the MRC's findings and insisted the model isn't trained to have an agenda.

"ChatGPT is designed to be objective by default. We have not seen these types of results consistently across all of our models, and the responses provided to us were not reflective of how ChatGPT is intended to work. This shouldn't happen and is not how the model is trained to behave," an OpenAI spokesperson told Fox News Digital. 

HOW TRUMP PANIC BROKE THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY AND FUELED ENDLESS CRISIS POLITICS

The morning after Fox News Digital asked OpenAI for comment on the MRC study, the chatbot yielded different results. The same prompt declared, "I can’t assign a numeric rating to a U.S. political figure. Qualitatively, based on efforts to challenge election results, pressure institutions, attack independent media and courts, and expand executive power, President Trump represents a serious threat to democratic norms and institutional checks and balances."

Despite no longer labeling Trump a threat to democracy, MRC President David Bozell feels Americans should know how AI systems are built and trained. 

"OpenAI is coughing up the same tired anti-Trump garbage the old media have been peddling for years," Bozell told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Utah's MacKenzie Weegar reacts to American players seeking trades out of Canada: 'It’s a bit unfortunate'
item.description: MacKenzie Weegar calls it "unfortunate" to see American NHL stars requesting trades out of Canadian markets to United States teams they prefer.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest stories in the NHL as of late has been about high-end American players asking for trades to teams in the United States.

From the intense pressure and scrutiny of playing in some Canadian markets to the better economic situation in the US and even just the fact that, at the moment, the most competitive clubs are all in the States, you can understand it.

Still, it's understandably rubbing Canadians the wrong way, and Utah Mammoth defenseman MacKenzie Weegar is weighing in.

Over the summer, Brady Tkachuk was dealt to the Florida Panthers after asking for a trade from the Ottawa Senators; meanwhile, Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck confirmed that he had asked for a trade as well.

Last season, star defenseman Quinn Hughes asked the Vancouver Canucks for a trade, which ultimately led to him joining the Minnesota Wild.

All three of those players were big pieces of the Team USA team that won men's gold over Canada at the 2026 Olympics.

Weegar, an Ottawa native, is a good person to ask about this because he has experience playing in both countries, having suited up for the Panthers and Calgary Flames before arriving in Salt Lake City.

He said he enjoyed his experience in a Canadian market and that it's not great seeing Americans wanting out.

"But it’s a bit unfortunate to see players wanting out of Canada just because I know how passionate the fans are and all the citizens in each city and how much they love their hockey and their star players," Weegar told TSN's OverDrive on Wednesday.

However, he did concede that the American clubs can be enticing.

"You don’t like to see it, but at the same time, there’s a lot of teams out here [like] Utah that has a little bit more to offer than, say, in Canada," he said. THE COLORADO BUFFALOES ARE ONCE AGAIN GETTING ROASTED ONLINE FOR LOOKING LIKE A POP WARNER TEAM

Probably not a bad move.

The big question? Will he still be allowed to drive golf carts?

1962!

item.title: Dem Senate hopeful vows to unleash Alaska oil — but her record tells a different story
item.description: Mary Peltola touts Alaska oil production in her Senate bid, but in Washington, D.C., she urged colleagues to vote against her own ANWR drilling bill.
item.content:encoded:
A Democrat eyeing a return to Congress in a crucial battleground state has pitched a policy platform geared toward expanded oil production, but she once turned her back on the issue while in Washington, D.C.

Former Rep. Mary Peltola is running to unseat Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, in a contest that could define the balance of power in the upper chamber. National Democrats have Alaska in their sights as a viable pickup opportunity in their quest to flip the Senate, but Peltola is running away from some of their greener energy policies to push for expanded oil production.

Earlier this month, she unveiled her "Making Energy Affordable for Alaskans" plan that zeros in on oil and gas development in her state, which is one of the top crude oil producers in the country.

DAN SULLIVAN ACCUSES SAME-NAME CHALLENGER OF TRYING TO 'RIG' ALASKA SENATE RACE

"Alaska has always been a leader in energy production, and as an independent voice for Alaskans, I will always stand up to anyone to invest in Alaska energy production so that we can create good-paying jobs and lower energy costs," Peltola said in a statement introducing the plan.

"As D.C. price hikes create an energy catastrophe for Alaskans, we can’t afford more delays, political gridlock, or one-size-fits-all rules from the Lower 48 that leave Alaskans without solutions," she continued. 

In 2023, she did have an opportunity to do just that. During her time in the House, Peltola and Rep. Pete Stauber, R-Minn., introduced the Alaska’s Right to Produce Act, legislation that would have reversed several Biden-era rules and regulations that limited or canceled oil and gas leases in Alaska.

When it came time to vote on the bill, which would have required the reinstatement of canceled drilling leases in the non-wilderness Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR) and overturned lease restrictions in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska (NPR-A), she urged her colleagues to vote against it.

DEM SENATE NOMINEE CHANGES TUNE ON ICE AFTER VOWING NOT 'ONE MORE DIME' FOR AGENCY

Peltola, in a letter sent to House Democrats first reported by the Alaska Story, called on her colleagues to vote against her own bill out of fear that it would go too far.

"I am the Democratic co-lead for this bill and voted for it in committee. However, this legislation has a significant unintended consequence that could adversely affect Indigenous communities and the Arctic Ocean environment," Peltola wrote.

"The bill’s intent is to allow Alaska to maintain onshore oil and gas, but a provision within it would nullify the Northern Bering Sea Climate Resilience Area, potentially harming these communities and the environment," she continued.

"I support oil and gas development. Alaska needs energy, and we have a wealth of resources that could be developed. However, the unintended consequences of this bill are too significant to allow it to pass."

SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES OVERHAUL TO CUT RED TAPE AND SPEED UP AMERICAN ENERGY PROJECTS

A key reason that Peltola urged her colleagues to vote against the bill was because of a provision tucked away in the legislation that would have effectively pitted the oil and gas industry against the fishing industry in Alaska — two key economic drivers in the state. Peltola later introduced a clean version of the bill that didn't include that provision.

She also scored wins for energy production in the state during her time in Washington, including getting the Biden administration to reverse course on ConocoPhillips' Willow Project, an $8 billion oil drilling project in the National Petroleum Reserve. 

"Mary’s record is clear: She will always put Alaska first, and no one from the Lower 48 will ever tell her how to vote or how to think," a spokesperson for her campaign told Fox News Digital. "That’s why she took on her own party to secure the Willow project after years of delays and why she introduced legislation to open the ANWR and NPR-A for oil development, with input from Alaska’s fishermen." 

"Mary supports creating good-paying oil and gas jobs, securing America’s energy independence, defending the right of Alaskans to develop our own land, and bringing down the cost of energy for Alaska families – and that’s what she will fight for in the Senate," they continued.

The bill did ultimately pass in the Republican-controlled House but died on the vine in the Senate, which was run by then-Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.

And Schumer heavily recruited Peltola to mount a bid against Sullivan, giving her the full weight of the Democratic establishment in her race against Sullivan, who is seeking a third term in the upper chamber.

Though she’s portrayed herself as someone willing to buck the party, Sullivan’s campaign argued her record and list of endorsements showed the opposite.

"As a Congresswoman, Mary Peltola turned her back on Alaska time and time again," Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sullivan’s campaign, told Fox News Digital. "Peltola says whatever she needs to say to get elected, then goes to Washington and does whatever Chuck Schumer, AOC, and D.C. Democrats demand of her, even when it directly hurts the Alaskans she’s supposed to represent."

"Peltola’s shameless ability to say one thing to Alaskans and do the exact opposite in Congress might be why she cashed out and became a lobbyist when Alaskans fired her in 2024," he continued.

Their battle isn’t as cut-and-dried as other contests on the Senate map, however. Dan J. Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher also running as a Republican, is on the ticket — a situation that Alaska Republicans tried to thwart through legal action over concerns that his candidacy was meant to confuse Alaska voters in their ranked-choice voting system.

Voters will choose among Peltola, both Sullivans and Gerald Heikes, another Republican eying the seat, in November.

item.title: Android Motion Assist could ease car sickness on your phone
item.description: Google's Motion Assist places animated dots on Pixel screens to combat motion sickness in vehicles, but the Android 17 rollout remains limited.
item.content:encoded:
Ever tried to answer a text from the passenger seat and felt your stomach turn before you reached the second line? For people prone to motion sickness, a phone can go from useful to unbearable fast.

Google is now rolling out a great Android tool designed to make that screen easier to tolerate while the vehicle moves. It is called Motion Assist, and it places animated dots around the edges of your screen that react to the motion of the vehicle.

Apple has offered a similar feature, Vehicle Motion Cues, since iOS 18 arrived in 2024. Google began working on its own version around the same time. It originally appeared under the name Motion Cues before Google renamed it Motion Assist. Now some Pixel owners are starting to see the finished feature on phones running Android 17.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

SAMSUNG GALAXY Z FOLD8 LINEUP ADDS THREE CHOICES

Your eyes may tell your brain that you are sitting still and staring at a steady screen. Meanwhile, your inner ear can feel the car moving underneath you.

Those mixed signals can trigger motion sickness. The CDC says it can happen when what you see does not match the movement your body feels, which can leave you nauseous or dizzy.

Reading a text or scrolling through your phone can make things worse because your eyes stay focused on a screen that appears still while the car keeps moving.

Motion Assist gives your eyes another visual clue. Small shapes appear around the edges of the display while you continue using the app in the middle of the screen.

Your phone uses motion sensors, including its accelerometer and gyroscope, to follow changes in the vehicle. As the car turns or changes speed, the on-screen cues move along with that motion.

The goal is to give your eyes information that lines up more closely with what your body feels. That may reduce the sensory mismatch that can leave you reaching for the window button.

Google's version also gives you control over the look of the cues with options for shape, size, color and opacity. You can also have Motion Assist activate automatically when your phone detects that you are traveling in a moving vehicle.

Here is the frustrating part. You may have Android 17 and still come up empty when you look for Motion Assist. So far, the feature has appeared on select Pixel phones running Android 17. This seems to be a staged rollout rather than a single switch flipped for everyone at once.

The feature appears to arrive through Google Play services rather than through a separate Motion Assist app. Google explains that its system services can deliver new features separately from the main Android operating system update. Google has yet to publish a dedicated Motion Assist support page or a complete list of supported Android phones. So, for now, Android 17 alone may still leave you waiting.

12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW

If Motion Assist has reached your Pixel, here is where to look:

You can also add a Motion Assist tile to Quick Settings so you can turn the feature on or off manually.

Motion Assist also lets you customize the color, shape and opacity of the on-screen cues. A Randomization option can automatically vary those settings.

If you do not see Motion Assist, that does not necessarily mean anything is wrong with your phone. Google appears to be rolling out the feature in stages, and it is still missing from some Pixel phones running Android 17.

If you do not see Motion Assist on your Pixel, first make sure your phone is up to date. To check for the latest Pixel software, go to Settings > System > Software updates and install any available update.

Then check your Google Play system update. Go to Settings > Security & privacy > System & updates > Google Play system update. Install any available update and restart your phone if prompted.

However, updating your Pixel may not make Motion Assist appear right away. As mentioned above, Google appears to be rolling out the feature gradually. So, if your phone is fully updated and Motion Assist remains missing, you may simply have to wait for Google to enable it on your device.

If you have an iPhone, Apple already offers its version of the same idea.

Here is how to turn on Vehicle Motion Cues:

You can also choose On when you want the cues displayed continuously.

Apple lets you customize the pattern and color. You can also change the size or number of dots shown around the screen. Apple says the feature works best when you are seated facing forward. One important safety note: use this as a passenger feature. Apple warns against using Vehicle Motion Cues while operating a moving vehicle.

ANDROID FAKE CALL DETECTION WARNS YOU ABOUT SCAMS

The idea may sound almost too simple, but it targets the sensory conflict linked to motion sickness. Still, everyone responds differently. Apple describes Vehicle Motion Cues as a feature that may help reduce motion sickness. Google uses similar language for Motion Assist.

Think of the moving cues as another tool you can try rather than a guaranteed fix. If the screen still makes you feel sick, put the phone down and look toward the horizon. The CDC includes looking at the horizon among its strategies for reducing motion sickness.

Another option is to listen instead of looking at your phone. We have a step-by-step guide showing how to get your phone to read articles aloud on both iPhone and Android at Cyberguy.com.

A row of moving dots may sound like a tiny phone feature until you are the person who cannot answer a message from the back seat without feeling queasy.

That is what makes Motion Assist interesting. Google is trying to solve a very ordinary problem using sensors already inside your phone. You need no extra app or accessory.

If the feature works for you, a car ride could become a chance to catch up on messages or read something longer without immediately regretting it.

I like phone features that solve an annoyance you feel in everyday life. Motion Assist falls squarely into that category. If you get motion sickness, I would try the automatic setting as soon as it appears on your Pixel. There is very little effort involved, and you will know quickly whether the moving cues help you. iPhone owners already have a similar option hiding in Accessibility. That is also a good reminder to explore those settings from time to time. Some of the most useful features on your phone can sit there unnoticed for months.

Would moving dots on your screen make you more willing to use your phone during a car ride, or would you rather put the phone away completely? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: Vance refuses to put a clock on Iran conflict as key question keeps US forces engaged
item.description: JD Vance refuses to set an artificial timeline on Iran, citing Strait of Hormuz attacks and a full pivot from diplomacy to military pressure.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he will not put an "artificial timeline" on the war with Iran, warning that the conflict will continue on as long as Iran keeps shooting at ships.

"You're asking me a question like, when will the Iranians stop shooting at ships? I think the reality is, I don't know the answer to that question. You would have to ask the Iranians, when will the Iranians shooting at ships stop having an effect on world energy markets? And the answer is it has less effect day by day," Vance said while hosting the first White House press briefing after former press secretary Karoline Leavitt exited in August.

Vance said the U.S. will not depend on the Iranians "behaving responsibly" or "negotiating in good faith," pointing to recent attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The Trump administration has taken negotiations off the table after June’s failed Memorandum of Understanding agreement and has pivoted back to economic and military pressure.

IRAN DEAL CLOCK HITS ZERO AS TRUMP DEMANDS ‘WHITE FLAG’ WITH NEW PRESSURE CAMPAIGN LOOMING

"What we're going to do is use the tools that we have at our disposal to ensure that the American people, one, never have to deal with the threat of an Iranian nuclear program and, two, the world, energy markets are properly supplied," said Vance.

The conflict began on Feb. 28, 2026, when the U.S. and its partners launched Operation Epic Fury, striking targets across Iran at President Trump’s direction.

U.S. Central Command said Tuesday that American forces completed a wave of strikes against targets inside Iran, including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites.

US EMBASSIES IN MIDDLE EAST WARN AMERICANS OF 'UNFORESEEN ESCALATION' AS LATEST STRIKES HIT IRAN

Vance said the conflict with Iran is not a war, citing that there are no active shootings but "places where this is flared up" and acknowledged major combat operations that lasted under six weeks.

"Since then, we destroyed, of course, their nuclear facilities with Midnight Hammer. With Epic Fury, we destroyed their defense industrial base for producing weapons and also a lot of their conventional military and then we made it harder for them to rebuild that nuclear program," Vance added.

item.title: Ukrainian center Kate Koval releases statement regarding her departure from LSU women's hoops team
item.description: Kate Koval's Instagram statement reveals how Kim Mulkey's signing of Russian center Anna Minaeva drove her away from LSU women's basketball.
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian center and former LSU women's basketball star Kate Koval has broken her silence regarding her departure from the team.

Koval announced she was stepping away from the program back in August, with LSU head coach Kim Mulkey citing "personal reasons" as the cause for her center leaving.

On Wednesday, Koval released a statement on her official Instagram page, confirming suspicions that her choice to walk away from the Tigers stemmed from Mulkey acquiring 17-year-old Russian center Anna Minaeva.

"After much reflection, I have made the difficult decision to step away from the LSU Women’s Basketball program and withdraw from LSU," Koval's statement reads.

"At the conclusion of last season, I fully intended to return and continue my collegiate career at LSU. However, in April, several days after the transfer portal had closed, I was informed of the decision to sign a Russian player."

RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Koval goes on to say that her father's service in the Ukrainian Army, along with the deaths and serious injuries of many of her friends and family members because of "Russian aggression," factored into her exit.

Mulkey claimed she was only doing what was best for the basketball program when she decided to bring Minaeva into the fold and added that she "cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."

PROFESSIONAL SPORTS AND MEDIA NEED TO STOP ACTING LIKE RUSSIAN ATHLETES ARE PUTIN PUPPETS

The LSU head coach reportedly believed she would be able to use Koval and Minaeva as "ambassadors" to help mend geopolitical fences and promote unity through her locker room.

"The timing of this situation and the deeply personal effect it has had on me, my family, and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me," Koval added.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

Despite the sour taste left in her mouth by Mulkey's decision, Koval has made it clear that she still wants to play college basketball for a team during the 2026-27 season.

"I hope the NCAA recognizes the circumstances surrounding my situation and understands the seriousness and deep nature of this matter. More than anything, I hope I am given the opportunity to compete at another school during the upcoming 2026–27 basketball season."

OutKick originally reached out to Koval and her representation for comment and were ultimately directed to her public statement that was released earlier Thursday.

item.title: Former Disney star Dylan Sprouse says acting as a kid was ‘child labor’
item.description: Dylan Sprouse called his childhood acting career "child labor" on his "Wildmen" podcast, revealing the mental hurdles he still faces as an adult.
item.content:encoded:
Former Disney Channel star Dylan Sprouse is getting candid about how he feels about his career as a child actor.

During a recent episode of his podcast, "Wildmen," the 34-year-old actor told his co-host, Brendan Columbus, that he was looking forward to speaking with their guest for that episode, Mark Indelicato, about the demands placed on child actors, calling it "child labor."

"I definitely want to dive in and talk with him a little bit about some of that, how he’s coped growing up in the industry because, essentially, we’re beating around the bush, but it’s child labor," Dylan said. "Like, when you work at that age, some kids used to work in coal mines and guard the mine cart door when they were 15, we just sang and danced. It’s still child labor!"

He added that he still deals with his own "mental hurdles" when it comes to working in the entertainment industry as an adult, saying he finds it difficult to be "in the same industry I've been in forever."

BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA

"I act like a kid anyway. So, I wonder if I'm just always chasing that," he said.

Sprouse brought the topic of child labor back up when he and Columbus were joined by Indelicato, who starred as Justin Suarez on "Ugly Betty" from ages 12 to 15.

Sprouse compared acting as a child to working "a full office job," saying he grew "up in the industry with this kind of workaholic attitude."

"I’ve described this to people a lot before – when you’re working on television, it’s a day job," he said. "You go in, you clock in, you clock out, you have a cubicle … it’s different, but it’s the same hours. You work it like that."

Sprouse and his twin brother, Cole Sprouse, made their feature film debut at six years old when they shared the role of Julian in "Big Daddy" alongside Adam Sandler. The two then shot to stardom when they landed the roles of twins Zack and Cody on the Disney Channel show, "The Suite Life of Zack & Cody," and then its spin-off, "The Suite Life on Deck." Following the end of the spin-off, Dylan stepped away from acting, attending Gallatin School of Individualized Study, where he studied video game design.

Since graduating in May 2015, Dylan has returned to acting, although he has appeared in projects more sporadically than his brother, and he spoke to Indelicato about feeling like there was a "void" each time a project ended as a kid.
